day_shape: 80 items: EU/UK joint condemnation of Iranian hybrid attacks and Hormuz strikes, Quad IAEA statement on Iran safeguards, Iraq retakes Kataib Hezbollah stronghold Jurf al-Sakhar, Houthi missile damages Riyadh's tallest tower, JPost reports mooted US-Israel strike within two weeks, IRGC names Iran International a military target.

threads.label: European pressure on Iran nuclear and hybrid threats
threads.summary: The EU and UK issued a joint Brussels statement demanding Iran halt 'hybrid attacks on European soil' and Strait of Hormuz strikes, while France, Germany, UK and US delivered a Quad statement to the IAEA Board of Governors on Iran's NPT safeguards. UK military cyber command told Sky News it is running offensive cyber operations against Iran, Russia, China and North Korea; two men were charged over September's RAF Fairford incident London prosecutors link to Iran.

threads.label: Reported US-Israel strike planning on Iran
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Israel and the US are weighing a new military assault on Iran, with former Navy commander Marom quoted predicting a joint strike within two weeks, while Senate Republicans rejected legislation requiring Trump to seek congressional approval. JPost also reported Netanyahu tasked Mossad chief Roman Gofman with an Iran operation bypassing IDF Chief of Staff Zamir, and B-2 pilots detailed Operation Midnight Hammer; Iran denied US chemical/biological weapons claims.

threads.label: Houthi-Saudi escalation on Red Sea
threads.summary: A Houthi missile damaged Riyadh's tallest building, hitting the PIF headquarters in the second attack on the financial district this month, while spokesman Yahya Saree warned Saudi airspace outside Mecca and Medina was unsafe within hours. The Houthis threatened to strike Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports if Hodeidah is attacked, per Defa Press, IRIB and Jerusalem Post.

threads.label: Iraq retakes Kataib Hezbollah stronghold
threads.summary: Iraqi security forces began deploying in Jurf al-Sakhar, held for over a decade by Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah, under a Shiite-brokered deal days after Quds Force chief arrived in Baghdad. The compromise was reported by Iran International and Jerusalem Post citing Reuters and three senior security officials.

threads.label: IDF strikes in Gaza and Lebanon
threads.summary: The IDF said it killed three Islamic Jihad and Hamas Nukhba commanders in Gaza over the past week, including Ahmad Abu Armana, and demolished a Hamas tunnel crossing the Yellow Line, while striking an underground Hezbollah missile-production site at Janta in the Beqaa. The IDF also published evidence it says identifies slain photojournalist Rushdi Sarraj as a Hamas operative, and reported 99,900+ tents and 9,000+ winter-supply trucks entered Gaza.

threads.label: Regime defiance messaging on war and Hormuz
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted that the Strait of Hormuz had ended the 'myth of American invincibility', while IRGC Commander Vahidi told the Liberation Vanguards Congress Iran controls 500km beyond the Persian Gulf and Araghchi joked there would be 'no war tonight'. Defa Press carried Makhber claiming the Shenzhen meeting showed America cannot assemble an anti-Iran coalition, alongside Tehran Friday prayer and Basij mobilisation messaging targeting 3.4 million students.

threads.label: Iran oil exports, domestic repression and IRGC threats
threads.summary: A tanker loaded Iranian crude in the Persian Gulf as Tehran weighed resuming exports despite a US naval blockade, while the IEA warned Hormuz disruption could cut global oil demand over 4% by 2035. Iran sentenced taekwondo champion Pouya Fakhrabadi to death over January's Yazd protests, and IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi named London-based Iran International among the armed forces' military targets.
